Lane County Circuit Court

Address

Lane County Circuit Court – Family Division
125 E 8th Ave, Eugene, OR 97401, United States

Operating Hours

  • Monday – Friday: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Saturday & Sunday: Closed

Contact Information

  • Phone: +1 541-682-4020
  • Website: Lane County Circuit Court

Circuit courts are the primary trial courts in the United States, handling a wide range of cases at the state level. They have general jurisdiction, which means they can hear and decide cases involving nearly any subject matter. The Lane County Circuit Court is one such court located in Eugene, Oregon, serving the residents of Lane County.

The Jurisdiction of Lane County Circuit Court

The Lane County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over a variety of cases, including:

Criminal Cases

These cases involve the prosecution of individuals charged with committing crimes. The court has the authority to hear both misdemeanors and felonies, which can range from minor offenses like traffic violations to serious crimes such as murder.

see also Garfield Heights Municipal Court

Civil Cases

Civil cases involve disputes between private parties, including individuals, businesses, and government entities. This can include personal injury claims, contract disputes, property disputes, and more.

Family Law Cases

Family law cases deal with matters related to family relationships, such as divorce, child custody and support, adoption, and guardianship.

Probate and Estate Cases

Probate and estate cases involve the administration of a deceased person's estate, including the distribution of assets to heirs and the payment of any outstanding debts.

The Structure of Lane County Circuit Court

Judges

The Lane County Circuit Court is composed of several judges who are elected to six-year terms. These judges are responsible for presiding over cases, making rulings, and ensuring that the proceedings are fair and just.

Court Staff

In addition to the judges, the court employs a variety of staff members, including clerks, court reporters, bailiffs, and other support staff. These individuals work together to ensure the efficient operation of the court and provide assistance to the judges and litigants.

Courtroom Procedures

The procedures in the Lane County Circuit Court are governed by the Oregon Rules of Civil Procedure and the Oregon Rules of Criminal Procedure. These rules establish guidelines for the conduct of trials, the presentation of evidence, and other aspects of the legal process.

Navigating the Lane County Circuit Court System

Filing a Case

To initiate a case in the Lane County Circuit Court, you must file the appropriate paperwork with the court clerk's office. This typically includes a complaint or petition, along with any required supporting documents and fees. Once filed, the case will be assigned to a judge and scheduled for future hearings.

Finding Legal Help

If you need assistance navigating the legal process in the Lane County Circuit Court, there are resources available to help. The Oregon State Bar offers a lawyer referral service, and there are legal aid organizations that provide low-cost or free legal services to eligible individuals. Additionally, the court's website contains helpful information and resources for self-represented litigants.

Online Resources

The Lane County Circuit Court offers a variety of online resources to help individuals navigate the court system. These resources include access to court records, forms, fee schedules, and information on court programs and services. By utilizing these tools, individuals can better understand and navigate the legal process.

Lane County Circuit Court Case Search

To search for a case in the Lane County Circuit Court, you can use the Oregon Judicial Department's (OJD) online case search system called OJCIN (Oregon Judicial Case Information Network). This system allows you to search for case information by name, case number, or attorney information. Access to OJCIN may require a subscription or a fee for individual case record searches. The link to OJCIN can be found on the Lane County Circuit Court's website.

Lane County Circuit Court Phone Number

The phone number for the Lane County Circuit Court is (541) 682-4201. You can call this number to reach the court clerk's office for general inquiries, case information, or assistance with court procedures.

Lane County Circuit Court Records

Court records for the Lane County Circuit Court can be accessed through the OJCIN system or by visiting the court clerk's office in person. Some records may be restricted or confidential, and a fee may be required for obtaining copies of court documents.

Lane County Court Records Smart Search

The Lane County Court Records Smart Search is a reference to the OJCIN system that allows users to search for court records and case information for the Lane County Circuit Court.

Lane County Court Judges

The judges in Lane County Circuit Court are elected to six-year terms and are responsible for presiding over cases, making rulings, and ensuring fair and just proceedings. The list of current judges can be found on the Lane County Circuit Court's website.

Lane County Circuit Court Divorce Records

Divorce records for the Lane County Circuit Court can be accessed through the OJCIN system or by visiting the court clerk's office. Some divorce records may be restricted or confidential, and fees may apply for obtaining copies of documents.

Lane County Court Forms

Court forms for the Lane County Circuit Court can be found on the court's website. These forms cover a wide range of case types and procedures, including civil, criminal, family law, and probate matters.

Lane County Circuit Court Small Claims

The Lane County Circuit Court handles small claims cases involving disputes of $10,000 or less. Information on how to file a small claims case, as well as required forms, can be found on the court's website.

Lane County Arraignments

Arraignments are the initial hearings in criminal cases where the defendant is informed of the charges against them and enters a plea. In Lane County, arraignments take place at the Lane County Circuit Court.

Lane County Criminal Records

Criminal records in Lane County can be accessed through the Oregon State Police's Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) division. In addition to CJIS, the OJCIN system can be used to search for criminal case information in the Lane County Circuit Court.

Please note that access to some records and information may be restricted, and fees may apply for obtaining copies of documents or for using certain online search services.

Conclusion

The Lane County Circuit Court plays a crucial role in the administration of justice in Lane County, Oregon. With jurisdiction over a wide variety of cases, the court serves as a vital institution for the resolution of disputes and the enforcement of the law. Understanding the structure and procedures of the court, as well as available resources, can help individuals successfully navigate the legal system.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. What types of cases does the Lane County Circuit Court handle?

The court handles criminal, civil, family law, and probate cases, among others.

  1. How can I find legal help for my case in the Lane County Circuit Court?

You can contact the Oregon State Bar's lawyer referral service, seek assistance from legal aid organizations, or use online resources provided by the court.

  1. Where is the Lane County Circuit Court located?

The court is located in Eugene, Oregon.

  1. How do I file a case in the Lane County Circuit Court?

To file a case, submit the appropriate paperwork, supporting documents, and fees to the court clerk's office.

  1. What online resources are available for the Lane County Circuit Court?

The court's website offers access to court records, forms, fee schedules, and information on court programs and services.
